nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r < k$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $\binom{k-i}{r-i} \mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0 \le i < r$, there is a Steiner system $S(r, k, n)$: a family $F$ of $k$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that every $r$-element subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is contained in exactly one member of $F$.
nodes.title: Keevash's existence theorem for Steiner systems

nodes.summary: The statement that for all natural numbers $r < k$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $\binom{k-i}{r-i} \mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0 \le i < r$, there is a Steiner system $S(r, k, n)$: a family $F$ of $k$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that every $r$-element subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is contained in exactly one member of $F$ (Erdős Problem 722).
nodes.title: Existence conjecture for Steiner systems
